_comment: Reference snippet — NOT installed by ai-sync. Merge the permissions block into
Why: a subagent's `tools:` frontmatter is all-or-nothing per tool. It can grant or
withhold Bash, but it cannot express 'Bash, but only read commands'. The reviewing
role agents (qa, architect, product, engineering-manager) need Bash to run a test
suite and read git metadata, so their read-only guarantee is otherwise enforced only
by instructions in the agent body. These deny rules make it real.
Scope caveat: permissions in settings.json apply to the WHOLE project, not per-agent.
These rules will also block you from running these commands in a normal session. If
your workflow needs any of them, drop that line rather than the whole block — and if
you routinely commit from inside Claude Code, this block is not for you.
ciso and planner need no rules here: they are granted no Bash at all, which is a
harder guarantee than any deny list. developer is intentionally unconstrained; it is
the one role meant to change the repo, and it only runs on explicit human approval.
